title: Finite-group BF state sums, gauge groupoids and gluing

items.title: Finite groupoid cardinality and homotopy-fiber integration
items.design_state: Locally authored A-page prerequisite or intermediate result required by the assigned finite-group BF proof route; complete statement and proof are recorded on the owning page.
items.statement:
A **finite groupoid** is a small category in which every morphism is invertible, with finitely many isomorphism classes and a finite automorphism group at every object. Write $\pi_0(\mathcal C)$ for its set of isomorphism classes. Its **groupoid cardinality** is

$$|\mathcal C|:=\sum_{[c]\in\pi_0(\mathcal C)}\frac{1}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(c)|}.$$

For an isomorphism-invariant function $f:\pi_0(\mathcal C)\to\mathbb C$, define

$$\int_{c\in\mathcal C} f(c):=\sum_{[c]\in\pi_0(\mathcal C)}\frac{f(c)}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(c)|}.$$

For finite groupoids $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$, a functor $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, and an object $d$ of $\mathcal D$, its **homotopy fiber** $\mathcal C_d$ has objects $(c,\alpha)$ with $\alpha:p(c)\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow}d$ and morphisms $u:(c,\alpha)\to(c',\alpha')$ satisfying $\alpha'\circ p(u)=\alpha$. Define pullback and pushforward of invariant functions by

$$(p^*g)([c])=g([p(c)]),\qquad (p_!f)([d])=\int_{(c,\alpha)\in\mathcal C_d} f([c]).$$

A span $\mathcal X\xleftarrow{a}\mathcal E\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal Y$ of finite groupoids therefore induces the linear map $b_!a^*$ on invariant functions.

references.title: Gregory W. Moore and Vivek Saxena, TASI Lectures on Topological Field Theories and Differential Cohomology
references.locator: §12, PDF pp. 50–51, for groupoids and automorphism groups; §§23.2–23.3, PDF pp. 92–99, for homotopy fiber products and finite pushforward by homotopy cardinality.

items.strategy: 1.1 The groupoid cardinality and integral in the Definition are finite sums by [A1]. Fix $d\in\mathcal D$ and one representative $c$ from each source isomorphism class. The set of isomorphisms $p(c)\cong d$ is empty or a torsor for the finite group $\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal D}(d)$. Every object of the homotopy fiber is isomorphic to one with such a chosen source representative, so the fiber has finitely many isomorphism classes. The automorphisms of $(c,\alpha)$ are the $u\in\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(c)$ satisfying $\alpha\circ p(u)=\alpha$, a subgroup of a finite group by [A1]. Thus every homotopy fiber is finite and each pushforward sum is finite. [given, A1]

items.title: Homotopy pullback of finite groupoids
items.design_state: Locally authored A-page definition required to specify finite homotopy-pullback objects and arrows used by span composition and boundary descent; complete statement and proof are recorded on the owning page.
items.statement:
Let $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $q:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ be functors of finite groupoids. The **homotopy pullback groupoid** $\mathcal C\times^h_{\mathcal D}\mathcal E$ has objects $(c,e,\alpha)$, where $c\in\mathcal C$, $e\in\mathcal E$, and $\alpha:p(c)\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow}q(e)$ is an isomorphism in $\mathcal D$. A morphism $(u,v):(c,e,\alpha)\to(c',e',\alpha')$ consists of isomorphisms $u:c\to c'$ and $v:e\to e'$ satisfying

$$q(v)\circ\alpha=\alpha'\circ p(u).$$

Composition is componentwise. The projections to $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal E$ send $(c,e,\alpha)$ to $c$ and $e$, respectively.

references.title: Gregory W. Moore and Vivek Saxena, TASI Lectures on Topological Field Theories and Differential Cohomology

items.strategy: 1.1 Identity pairs satisfy the compatibility equation. If $(u,v)$ and $(u',v')$ are composable compatible pairs, then $q(v'\circ v)\circ\alpha=q(v')\circ q(v)\circ\alpha=q(v')\circ\alpha'\circ p(u)=\alpha''\circ p(u'\circ u)$, so their composite is compatible. Inverting the compatibility equation shows $(u^{-1},v^{-1})$ is compatible with the reversed objects. Thus the stated data form a groupoid. [given, F1, algebra]

items.title: Finite flat connection groupoid on a cell complex
items.design_state: Assigned planned interface; complete current statement and proof are recorded on the owning page.
items.statement:
Let $K$ be a finite connected CW complex and $G$ a finite group. Choose an orientation of each 1-cell and, for each 2-cell, its based attaching word in the finite edge presentation of $\pi_1(K)$; the choice of base paths is part of that presentation. A **flat edge assignment** is a label $g_e\in G$ for every oriented 1-cell with $g_{\bar e}=g_e^{-1}$, such that each attaching word has holonomy $1$. If a word traverses edges $e_1,\ldots,e_m$ in that order with exponents $\epsilon_j\in\{1,-1\}$, its holonomy is $g_{e_m}^{\epsilon_m}\cdots g_{e_1}^{\epsilon_1}$.

Write $\operatorname{Flat}(K,G)$ for the finite set of flat assignments and $K_0$ for the vertices. The finite vertex gauge group $G^{K_0}$ acts by

$$(h\cdot g)_e=h_{t(e)}g_eh_{s(e)}^{-1},$$

where $s(e)$ and $t(e)$ are the source and target vertices. The **finite flat connection groupoid** $\mathcal C_G(K)$ is the action groupoid $\operatorname{Flat}(K,G)//G^{K_0}$: its objects are flat assignments and its arrows $g\to g'$ are the $h\in G^{K_0}$ with $h\cdot g=g'$. Its untwisted finite BF partition function is the groupoid cardinality

$$Z_G(K):=|\mathcal C_G(K)|=\sum_{[g]\in\operatorname{Flat}(K,G)/G^{K_0}}\frac{1}{|\operatorname{Stab}(g)|} =\frac{|\operatorname{Flat}(K,G)|}{|G|^{|K_0|}}.$$

This is a finite combinatorial model; it has no continuous Lie-algebra-valued connection integral or additional cocycle phase.

For a finite disconnected CW complex, define $\mathcal C_G(K)$ to be the product of the groupoids of its connected components; for the empty complex use the terminal groupoid.

items.strategy: 1.1 Reversing an edge replaces $g_e$ by $g_e^{-1}$, and the gauge formula sends the reverse label to $(h_{t(e)}g_eh_{s(e)}^{-1})^{-1}=h_{s(e)}g_e^{-1}h_{t(e)}^{-1}$. For a closed attaching word based at a vertex $v$, the transformed holonomy is $h_v\operatorname{Hol}(w)h_v^{-1}$. Thus the inverse-edge rule and the flatness equations are preserved by every vertex gauge transformation. [given, F2, algebra]

items.title: Finite groupoid push-pull satisfies Fubini and adjunction
items.design_state: Locally authored A-page prerequisite or intermediate result required by the assigned finite-group BF proof route; complete statement and proof are recorded on the owning page.
items.statement:
Let $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ and $q:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Z$ be functors of finite groupoids. The iterated homotopy fiber over any $z\in\mathcal Z$ is equivalent to the homotopy fiber of $q\circ p$, so $(q\circ p)_!=q_!p_!$. Consequently, for composable spans of finite groupoids, the induced push-pull maps compose by the homotopy-pullback composite span. If $\mathcal X\xleftarrow{a}\mathcal E\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal Y$ is a span, equip invariant functions with

$$\langle f,g\rangle_{\mathcal X}:=\sum_{[x]\in\pi_0(\mathcal X)} \frac{\overline{f([x])}\,g([x])}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal X}(x)|}.$$

Then the adjoint of $b_!a^*$ is $a_!b^*$, the map of the transposed span.

references.title: Gregory W. Moore and Vivek Saxena, TASI Lectures on Topological Field Theories and Differential Cohomology
references.locator: §§23.2–23.3, PDF pp. 92–99, for homotopy pullbacks of correspondences and pushforward weighted by homotopy cardinality.

items.strategy: 1.1 For fixed $z\in\mathcal Z$, an object of the iterated fiber is $(y,\beta:q(y)\to z,x,\alpha:p(x)\to y)$. The functor $(y,\beta,x,\alpha)\mapsto(x,\beta\circ q(\alpha))$ maps it to $(\mathcal X)_z$. A quasi-inverse sends $(x,\gamma:q(p(x))\to z)$ to $(p(x),\gamma,x,\operatorname{id}_{p(x)})$. The composite on $(\mathcal X)_z$ is the identity. For any iterated object, the isomorphism $\alpha:p(x)\to y$ and $\operatorname{id}_x$ give a natural isomorphism from the quasi-inverse image back to that object. Hence the functor is an equivalence. [given, F1, construct]

items.title: Finite BF partition function is a topological invariant
items.design_state: Assigned planned interface; complete current statement and proof are recorded on the owning page.
items.statement:
Let $K$ be a finite CW complex, possibly disconnected, and let $G$ be a finite group. Write its connected components as $K_1,\ldots,K_m$ and choose a vertex $v_j$ in each. Let $\mathcal R_G(K)$ be the product over $j$ of the action groupoids whose objects are homomorphisms $\rho:\pi_1(K_j,v_j)\to G$ and whose arrows $\rho\to\rho'$ are elements $a\in G$ satisfying $\rho'(\gamma)=a\rho(\gamma)a^{-1}$ for every loop class $\gamma$; identity arrows are labeled by $1$, and if $a:\rho\to\rho'$ and $b:\rho'\to\rho''$, then their composite $b\circ a$ is labeled by $ba$. For $K=\varnothing$, this empty product is the terminal groupoid. Choosing a maximal tree in each component, inverse path holonomy defines an equivalence $\Phi_K:\mathcal C_G(K)\simeq\mathcal R_G(K)$: for an edge path traversing $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ with signs $\epsilon_k$, its holonomy is $H_A(e_1^{\epsilon_1}\cdots e_n^{\epsilon_n})=g_{e_n}^{\epsilon_n}\cdots g_{e_1}^{\epsilon_1}$, and $\Phi_K(A)$ sends a loop class represented by an edge loop $[\gamma]$ to $H_A(\bar\gamma)$; a gauge arrow $h$ maps to the conjugating arrow $h(v_j)$ on component $K_j$. In particular, for connected $K$,

$$|\mathcal C_G(K)|=\frac{|\operatorname{Hom}(\pi_1(K,v_1),G)|}{|G|},$$

and for arbitrary finite $K$,

$$|\mathcal C_G(K)|=\prod_{j=1}^{m}\frac{|\operatorname{Hom}(\pi_1(K_j,v_j),G)|}{|G|}.$$

The action retains all conjugation stabilizers. For a subcomplex inclusion $\jmath:L\hookrightarrow K$, choose a base vertex $v_i$ in each component $L_i$, a base vertex $w_{j(i)}$ in its containing component $K_{j(i)}$, and an edge path $\gamma_i$ in $K_{j(i)}$ from $w_{j(i)}$ to $v_i$. The associated based map is $\jmath_{\gamma_i,*}([\ell])=[\gamma_i*\jmath(\ell)*\bar\gamma_i]$. Under $\Phi_K$ and $\Phi_L$, restriction corresponds to precomposition by these maps, up to the natural isomorphism whose component at a flat assignment $A$ is conjugation by $H_A(\bar\gamma_i)$. Thus the partition function depends only on the fundamental-group representation groupoid, not on the chosen finite cell decomposition.

items.strategy: 1.1 Starting with any flat assignment, set the root gauge value at $v_0$ to the identity. Along the unique tree path from $v_0$, choose the gauge value at each new vertex so that the transformed label on the traversed tree edge is the identity; when that edge is traversed against its chosen orientation, use its inverse label. This recursively produces a tree-normalized assignment. It is unique among gauges whose value at $v_0$ is the identity, since the condition that each transformed tree label remain $1$ determines each next vertex value. [given, F1, construct]

items.title: Finite gauge state spaces and bordism spans
items.design_state: Locally authored A-page prerequisite or intermediate result required by the assigned finite-group BF proof route; complete statement and proof are recorded on the owning page.
items.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$ and a finite group $G$. A **triangulated $d$-bordism** $M:\Sigma_0\to\Sigma_1$ is a compact oriented piecewise-linear $d$-manifold with product collars on its boundary, where $\Sigma_0$ and $\Sigma_1$ are closed oriented $(d-1)$-manifolds with finite triangulations and the incoming boundary is identified with $-\Sigma_0$ while the outgoing boundary is identified with $\Sigma_1$. The boundary triangulations agree with the induced triangulation of $M$.

For a closed $(d-1)$-manifold $\Sigma$, define the state space

$$V_G(\Sigma):=\operatorname{Fun}(\pi_0(\mathcal C_G(\Sigma)),\mathbb C), \qquad \langle f,g\rangle_\Sigma :=\sum_{[A]\in\pi_0(\mathcal C_G(\Sigma))} \frac{\overline{f([A])}g([A])}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C_G(\Sigma)}(A)|}.$$

The orientation reversal $-\Sigma$ has the same underlying triangulated cell complex and the same chosen directions on its edges, with only the manifold orientation reversed. Since the flat-connection groupoid uses the cell complex, directed edge labels, flatness equations, and vertex gauge action, not the manifold orientation, the identity on these data gives $\mathcal C_G(-\Sigma)=\mathcal C_G(\Sigma)$ and hence the same function set for their state spaces. For a complex vector space $W$, write $\overline W$ for its conjugate vector space, with the same addition and scalar multiplication $\lambda\cdot_{\overline W}w:=\overline\lambda w$. The map $J_\Sigma:V_G(-\Sigma)\to\overline{V_G(\Sigma)}$ given by $J_\Sigma(f)=\overline f$ pointwise is complex-linear. Reversing the manifold orientation does not replace any fixed directed edge label by its inverse; inversion occurs only when a chosen edge direction itself is reversed.

The specified boundary triangulation identifications induce restriction functors. On the incoming end, $r_0$ is restriction to $\partial_{\mathrm{in}}M$, transport through its identification with $-\Sigma_0$, and then the identity on the common underlying cell data $\mathcal C_G(-\Sigma_0)=\mathcal C_G(\Sigma_0)$. The outgoing functor $r_1$ is defined by restriction and its specified identification with $\Sigma_1$. In either transport, a chosen edge mapped to the opposite chosen direction uses the inverse-edge rule from the flat-connection Definition. These functors give a span of finite groupoids

$$\mathcal C_G(\Sigma_0)\xleftarrow{r_0}\mathcal C_G(M)\xrightarrow{r_1}\mathcal C_G(\Sigma_1).$$

The associated linear map is

$$Z_M:=(r_1)_!r_0^*:V_G(\Sigma_0)\to V_G(\Sigma_1),$$

where pullback and pushforward are the finite homotopy-fiber operations just defined. For empty boundary, the amplitude is $Z_G(M)=|\mathcal C_G(M)|$.

items.strategy: 1.1 Each boundary and bulk triangulation has finitely many cells, and $G$ is finite. Thus the field sets and gauge groups in [F1] are finite, the boundary state spaces are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces, and the sums defining their pairings and amplitudes are finite. The displayed inner product is positive definite because every coefficient $1/|\operatorname{Aut}(A)|$ is a positive real number. [given, F1, F2]

items.title: Flat-connection groupoids satisfy boundary descent
items.design_state: Locally authored A-page prerequisite or intermediate result required by the assigned finite-group BF proof route; complete statement and proof are recorded on the owning page.
items.statement:
Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be compact triangulated $d$-bordisms glued along an identified closed triangulated boundary $\Sigma$, with collars and compatible triangulations. The finite flat-connection groupoid on the glued manifold is equivalent to the homotopy pullback groupoid

$$\mathcal C_G(M_2\cup_\Sigma M_1) \simeq \mathcal C_G(M_2)\times^h_{\mathcal C_G(\Sigma)}\mathcal C_G(M_1).$$

Writing $r_i:\mathcal C_G(M_i)\to\mathcal C_G(\Sigma)$ for restriction, a pullback object is $(A_2,A_1,\alpha:r_2(A_2)\cong r_1(A_1))$. A morphism $(u_2,u_1)$ to $(A_2',A_1',\alpha')$ satisfies $r_1(u_1)\circ\alpha=\alpha'\circ r_2(u_2)$.

items.strategy: 1.1 A global flat labeling on $M_2\cup_\Sigma M_1$ restricts to flat labelings on both pieces whose boundary labels agree. The identity boundary isomorphism makes this a triple in the homotopy pullback defined by [F3]. Restriction of a global vertex gauge transformation gives a compatible pair, so restriction defines a functor from the global groupoid. [given, F1, F2, F3, construct]

items.title: Finite gauge theory gluing is weighted push-pull
items.design_state: Assigned planned interface; complete current statement and proof are recorded on the owning page.
items.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$ and a finite group $G$. The state spaces and linear maps defined for compatible collared triangulated $d$-bordisms compose under gluing: if $M_1:\Sigma_0\to\Sigma_1$ and $M_2:\Sigma_1\to\Sigma_2$, then

$$Z_{M_2\cup_{\Sigma_1}M_1}=Z_{M_2}\circ Z_{M_1}.$$

The cylinder on $\Sigma$ acts as the identity on $V_G(\Sigma)$. Disjoint unions act by tensor products of state spaces and maps. Let $c_\Sigma:V_G(\Sigma)\to V_G(-\Sigma)$ be the anti-linear map $c_\Sigma(f)=\overline f$ under the common underlying groupoid of the orientation-reversed boundary. With the weighted inner products from the Definition, if $\overline M:-\Sigma_1\to-\Sigma_0$ denotes $M:\Sigma_0\to\Sigma_1$ with reversed orientation, then

$$Z_{\overline M}\circ c_{\Sigma_1}=c_{\Sigma_0}\circ Z_M^\dagger,$$

where $Z_M^\dagger$ is the adjoint of $Z_M$; equivalently, after the pointwise-conjugation identifications, orientation reversal gives the weighted adjoint. For a connected closed $d$-manifold $M$, its scalar amplitude is $|\operatorname{Hom}(\pi_1(M),G)|/|G|$.

items.title: Abelian finite BF counts on S³ and T³
items.design_state: Assigned planned interface; complete current statement and proof are recorded on the owning page.
items.statement:
For a finite abelian group $G$, the untwisted finite BF normalization gives

$$Z_G(S^3)=\frac1{|G|},\qquad Z_G(T^3)=|G|^2.$$

These scalar amplitudes need not equal one.

items.strategy: 1.1 Give $S^3$ its CW structure with one 0-cell and one 3-cell. Its 1-skeleton has no non-tree edges and it has no 2-cell relators, so [F2] gives $\pi_1(S^3)=1$. There is exactly one homomorphism from the trivial group to $G$, and [F1] gives $Z_G(S^3)=1/|G|$. [given, F1, F2, algebra]
